userStories.title: Record Bash process exit codes on durable tool-audit rows
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add optional Bash process exit codes to tool results and durable audit rows only when the shell exited on its own.

**Motivation** — A `grep` that finds nothing exits 1, as do `diff` when inputs differ and `test` when the condition is false. Each one is recorded as `outcome: "error"`, exactly like a crashed command.

**Approach** — Symbols this feature **reads** (unchanged):

- `runArgv` result (`src/utils/argv-exec.ts`): `exitCode: number`, `timedOut: boolean`, `aborted?: boolean`. An already-aborted signal resolves with `exitCode: -1` and `aborted: true`.
- `CommandLauncher.run` → `LaunchResult` (`src/sandbox/types.ts`): carries the same `exitCode` / `timedOut` / `aborted` plus `executed` and `sandbox`.
- `_bashToolDeps.runArgv` (`src/tools/bash.ts`): the test seam used when no launcher is passed.
- `createCodingToolRuntime` and `compileToolPolicy` (`src/tools`): `runtimeFor` in `test/unit/tools/runtime-sandbox-audit.test.ts` is the fixture to mirror.

Symbols this feature **changes**. The baseline exists only to locate the code; it is never the interface to implement.

- `ToolResult.audit` (`src/tools/registry.ts`)
  - Baseline: `{ executed; target?; sandbox? }`
  - Target: `{ executed; target?; sandbox?; exitCode? }`. The new field is `readonly exitCode?: number` and is set only by the Bash tool.
- `ToolCallRecord` (`src/tools/tool-audit.ts`)
  - Target: gains `readonly exitCode?: number`. Additive and optional, so `TOOL_AUDIT_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays `1`, as it did for `sandbox`.
- The runtime's internal `log(...)` audit parameter (`src/tools/runtime.ts`)
  - Target: accepts `exitCode?: number` and spreads it onto the `sink.record(...)` row only when defined. This is the same conditional-spread idiom used for `executed`, `target`, `approval` and `sandbox`.
- `createBashTool(...).run` (`src/tools/bash.ts`)
  - Target: the success return's `audit` object literal gains `exitCode: launched.exitCode` by conditional spread, the same idiom as `sandbox` in that literal. It is spread when neither `launched.timedOut` nor `launched.aborted === true`, and that includes the `orphansKilled` case. Otherwise the audit has no `exitCode` key.

`isError`, the result `content`, and the ledger `outcome` (`"ok" | "error" | "denied" | "denied:ask"`) are unchanged.

### Failure Handling

| Condition | Behavior |
|:--|:--|
| Command timed out (`timedOut: true`) | Audit has no `exitCode` key; `isError` stays `true` |
| Command aborted by the turn signal (`aborted: true`) | Audit has no `exitCode` key; `isError` stays `true` |
| Bash tool throws before a process result exists (catch path, e.g. sandbox wrap failure) | Unchanged: no `audit`, so the row has no `exitCode` |
| Call denied by policy (`denied`) | Row has no `exitCode` (the tool never ran) |
| Background processes killed after exit (`orphansKilled: true`) | Audit carries `exitCode` (the shell itself exited) |
| Any non-Bash tool | Row has no `exitCode` key |

**Scope** — In: change src/tools/bash.ts, src/tools/runtime.ts, src/tools/tool-audit.ts and src/tools/registry.ts; add test/unit/tools/bash-exit-code-audit.test.ts (runArgv seam, fake launcher, restore runArgv in afterEach as in test/unit/tools/after-tool-truncation.test.ts) and test/unit/tools/runtime-exit-code-audit.test.ts (recording sink mirroring runtimeFor, wildcard Bash policy seam, createToolAuditSink flush into makeTempDir(), restore runArgv in afterEach); update test/unit/tools/bash-sandbox.test.ts exact audit equality for echo hi with exitCode: 0 and executed/sandbox unchanged. Do not grow test/unit/tools/runtime.test.ts beyond its 650-line split target. Out: Changing `isError`, the model-facing result text, or the ledger `outcome` values. A negative answer stays `outcome: "error"`, and consumers read `exitCode` to tell the two apart. Recording exit codes for `RunCommand` or its `Exec` argv branch. Recording `exitCode` on command-safety shadow rows. Bumping `TOOL_AUDIT_SCHEMA_VERSION`. Any report, CLI or analytics reader of the new field.

**Interface** — `ToolResult.audit`: `{ executed; target?; sandbox?; exitCode? }`; `readonly exitCode?: number`. `ToolCallRecord`: `readonly exitCode?: number`. Runtime `log(...)` audit parameter: `exitCode?: number`.
acceptanceCriteria: When createBashTool().run({ command: "rg nomatch src" }, ctx) receives _bashToolDeps.runArgv resolving exitCode: 1, stdout: "", stderr: "", timedOut: false, then result.audit.exitCode is 1.
When that rg nomatch src call exits 1, then createBashTool().run returns isError: true, unchanged by this feature.
When that rg nomatch src call exits 1, then createBashTool().run returns content beginning with "exit 1", unchanged by this feature.
When createBashTool().run({ command: "echo hi" }, ctx) receives _bashToolDeps.runArgv resolving exitCode: 0, then result.audit.exitCode is 0.
When createBashTool().run({ command: "echo hi" }, ctx) receives _bashToolDeps.runArgv resolving exitCode: 0, then result.isError is false.
When createBashTool().run(...) receives _bashToolDeps.runArgv resolving exitCode: 2, then result.audit.exitCode is 2.
When createBashTool().run(...) receives _bashToolDeps.runArgv resolving timedOut: true and exitCode: 143, then result.audit has no exitCode key (checked with `in`).
When createBashTool().run(...) receives _bashToolDeps.runArgv resolving timedOut: true and exitCode: 143, then result.isError is true.
When createBashTool().run(...) receives _bashToolDeps.runArgv resolving aborted: true and exitCode: -1, then result.audit has no exitCode key (checked with `in`).
When createBashTool().run(...) receives _bashToolDeps.runArgv resolving aborted: true and exitCode: -1, then result.isError is true.
When createBashTool().run(...) receives _bashToolDeps.runArgv resolving exitCode: 0 and orphansKilled: true, then result.audit.exitCode is 0.
When createBashTool({ launcher }) has launcher.state: { kind: "disabled" } and launcher.run rejects with an Error, then its run result has isError: true.
When createBashTool({ launcher }) has launcher.state: { kind: "disabled" } and launcher.run rejects with an Error, then its run result has no audit key (checked with `in`).

When createBashTool({ launcher }) has launcher.state: { kind: "disabled" } and launcher.run resolves exitCode: 1, stdout: "", stderr: "", timedOut: false, executed: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "false"], and sandbox: { backend: "none", wrapped: false }, then its result.audit equals { executed: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "false"], sandbox: { backend: "none", wrapped: false }, exitCode: 1 }.
When createCodingToolRuntime with a recording sink calls a tool returning { content: "exit 1", isError: true, audit: { executed: ["x"], exitCode: 1 } }, then its recorded row has exitCode: 1.
When createCodingToolRuntime with a recording sink calls a tool returning { content: "exit 1", isError: true, audit: { executed: ["x"], exitCode: 1 } }, then its recorded row has outcome: "error".
When createCodingToolRuntime with a recording sink calls a tool returning { content: "exit 1", isError: true, audit: { executed: ["x"], exitCode: 1 } }, then its recorded row has executed: ["x"].
When createCodingToolRuntime with a recording sink calls a tool returning { content: "ok", audit: { executed: ["x"], exitCode: 0 } }, then its recorded row has exitCode: 0.
When createCodingToolRuntime with a recording sink calls a tool returning { content: "ok", audit: { executed: ["x"], exitCode: 0 } }, then its recorded row has outcome: "ok".
When createCodingToolRuntime calls a non-Bash tool returning { content: "ok" } with no audit, then its recorded row has no exitCode key (checked with `in`).
When a runtime built with compileToolPolicy([], root) and extraTools: [createBashTool()] calls callTool("Bash", { command: "echo hi" }), then its denied row has no exitCode key (checked with `in`).

When a runtime with a policy granting Bash pattern * and extraTools: [createBashTool()] calls callTool("Bash", { command: "rg nomatch src" }) with _bashToolDeps.runArgv resolving exitCode: 1 and empty stdout and stderr, then its recorded row has exitCode: 1.

When a runtime with a policy granting Bash pattern * and extraTools: [createBashTool()] calls callTool("Bash", { command: "rg nomatch src" }) with _bashToolDeps.runArgv resolving exitCode: 1 and empty stdout and stderr, then its recorded row has outcome: "error".
When createToolAuditSink records a row with exitCode: 1 and flushes to a JSON file, then the file's calls[0].exitCode is 1.

routing.reasoning: Four additive source edits thread one optional field through existing Bash and runtime audit spreads; new seam tests and one equality update fit a single TDD session without new architecture or security-policy changes. [A/B nax#2227: testStrategy overridden to three-session-tdd so test-writer/implementer/verifier are measured per role.]

modifiedFiles.reason: the exact-equality assertion on `r.audit` in "run: goes through the launcher and carries the sandbox record on audit" gains `exitCode: 0` for the `echo hi` call; `executed` and `sandbox` stay exactly as asserted.

analysis: This is an additive TypeScript/Bun change across the existing Bash-to-ledger pipeline. src/tools/bash.ts:219-290 defines createBashTool().run: without a launcher it uses injectable _bashToolDeps.runArgv; with a launcher it uses CommandLauncher.run; it formats content, determines isError from timeout/nonzero exit/abort, and returns audit with executed and optional sandbox; the catch returns isError without audit. src/utils/argv-exec.ts:37-49 defines ArgvExecResult (exitCode, timedOut, optional aborted/orphansKilled), and :146-150 gives an already-aborted signal sentinel exitCode -1; src/sandbox/types.ts:77-90 defines LaunchResult extending this result with executed and sandbox. src/tools/registry.ts:20-44 defines ToolResult.audit as executed plus optional target/sandbox; append optional readonly exitCode without requiring changes to other tool producers. src/tools/runtime.ts:215-290 declares log's audit parameter and conditionally spreads fields to sink.record; :346-434 passes result.audit via logCall, with outcome selected solely by result.isError. Its policy-denied path at :510-517 never executes the tool; its command-safety shadow tap at :353-365 uses approval/executed only and must not get exitCode. src/tools/tool-audit.ts:20-75 defines ToolCallRecord and :150-187 writes sink records to JSON using redactRowStrings; its schema version stays 1. Existing test seams: test/unit/tools/runtime-sandbox-audit.test.ts:10-46 builds a wildcard-granted runtime and recording sink, asserting field propagation and absence; test/unit/tools/after-tool-truncation.test.ts:27-45 saves/restores _bashToolDeps.runArgv and manages temporary directories; test/unit/tools/bash-sandbox.test.ts:62-75 has an exact audit equality assertion for echo hi that needs exitCode: 0 while retaining executed and sandbox, and :77-82 covers wrap failure; test/unit/tools/tool-audit.test.ts exercises JSON flush. New focused tests belong in the two specified new files, not test/unit/tools/runtime.test.ts (past its 650-line split target). Risks: nonzero exit must continue to set isError and outcome error, including ordinary negative answers; content must retain exit N; timeout/abort must omit the key rather than emit undefined or sentinel 143/-1; 0 must survive the conditional spread. Older files and non-Bash tools need no migration: their rows simply lack the optional field. Do not change RunCommand/Exec producers, shadow rows, output readers, policy, or schema version.
outOfScope: Changing `isError`, the model-facing result text, or the ledger `outcome` values. A negative answer stays `outcome: "error"`, and consumers read `exitCode` to tell the two apart.
Adding a new `outcome` value such as `"no-match"` or `"nonzero"`.
Recording exit codes for `RunCommand` or its `Exec` argv branch.
Any report, CLI or analytics reader of the new field.
`denied:ask` rows are not separately tested: an ask-denied call never runs the tool, so it never carries a tool `audit`.
